name_en: Aji no sanbai — grilled horse mackerel steeped whole in three-part vinegar
summary_ja: 焦げ目をつけて焼いたアジを、唐辛子や刻みしょうがを効かせた三杯酢に漬ける。酢が骨をやわらげ丸ごと食べられるようにする工夫で、小アジが出回る瀬戸内の夏祭りの酒肴として親しまれてきたという。
summary_en: Aji (horse mackerel) is grilled until lightly charred, then steeped in a three-part vinegar dressing sharpened with chili and ginger. The vinegar is said to soften the bones enough to eat whole, and the dish has long served as a summer festival accompaniment to drinks around the Seto Inland Sea.
source_title: アジの三杯 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Imotako — octopus and taro simmered together
summary_ja: 瀬戸内海でとれるタコと里芋を、だしと調味料でともに煮付けたシンプルな一品。かつては正月や婚礼などのハレの日のごちそうだったが、今は日常の惣菜としてよくつくられるという。
summary_en: Octopus from the Seto Inland Sea and taro are simmered together in a simple seasoned broth. Once reserved for New Year and wedding feasts, it is said to have become an everyday side dish today.
source_title: いもたこ 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kagawa konnyaku no shiraae — konjac dressed in sweet tofu-sesame miso
summary_ja: 短冊に切って炒めたこんにゃくを、すりつぶした豆腐とごま、味噌を合わせた衣で和える。食物繊維の多いこんにゃくを、悪運を払い無病息災を願う節分に食べる家庭が多いという。
summary_en: Konjac cut into strips and pan-fried is dressed in a paste of mashed tofu, sesame, and miso. Many households are said to eat this fiber-rich konjac dish on Setsubun, the seasonal turning-point believed to ward off misfortune for the year ahead.
source_title: こんにゃくの白あえ 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Manba no kenchan — winter mustard greens stir-fried with tofu
summary_ja: 霜にあたって甘みが増す冬の高菜「まんば」を煮干しと炒め、豆腐と油揚げを崩しながら加える。細切り野菜と豆腐を炒め合わせるけんちん料理がなまって「けんちゃん」と呼ばれるようになったという。
summary_en: Manba, a winter mustard green that sweetens after frost, is stir-fried with dried sardines, then crumbled tofu and fried tofu are worked in. The name kenchan is said to be a local slurring of kenchin, a dish of shredded vegetables stir-fried with tofu.
source_title: まんばのけんちゃん 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Sawasawa — konjac and sweet potato simmered into a thick soup
summary_ja: こんにゃくを人参やごぼうとともに出汁で煮て、すりおろしたさつまいもでとろみをつける三豊市仁尾町の郷土料理。汁気の多いさらさらとした食感が名の由来とされ、法事などの際につくられてきたという。
summary_en: Konjac is simmered in dashi with carrot and burdock, then thickened with grated sweet potato, in this dish from Nio, Mitoyo. Its name is said to come from the sara-sara texture of its brothy consistency, traditionally made for memorial services.
source_title: さわさわ 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kagawa shoyu mame — roasted dried fava beans steeped in seasoned soy sauce
summary_ja: 乾燥そら豆を煎ってから醤油、砂糖、唐辛子の調味液に漬け込む。煮豆と違い煎ってから漬けることで、噛むとポロッと崩れる食感になるという。香川の稲の裏作として栽培されるそら豆を使う保存食。
summary_en: Dried fava beans are roasted, then steeped in a soy sauce, sugar, and chili liquid. Unlike simmered beans, roasting first is said to give a crumbly bite when chewed — a preserved food built on fava beans grown as a second crop after Kagawa's rice.
source_title: しょうゆ豆 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Takuan no kinpira — aged pickled daikon desalted and stir-fried
summary_ja: 酸味の出た古漬けたくあんを水にさらして塩抜きし、油で炒めて赤唐辛子で仕上げる惣菜。冬にたくあんを大量に仕込む香川で、余さず食べ切る工夫として親しまれてきたという。
summary_en: Aged pickled daikon that has developed a sour edge is soaked to remove salt, then stir-fried in oil and finished with red chili. Said to have taken hold in Kagawa, where households pickle large batches of daikon each winter, as a way to use every last piece.
source_title: たくあんのきんぴら 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Teppai — freshwater carp and daikon dressed in white miso vinegar
summary_ja: ため池でとれるフナを塩と酢でしめ、大根とともに讃岐の白味噌でつくった酢味噌で和える。フナを「鉄砲」と呼んだことから「鉄砲和え」がなまり「てっぱい」になったとされる冬の酒肴。
summary_en: Crucian carp from irrigation ponds is cured in salt and vinegar, then dressed with daikon in a vinegared white miso from Sanuki. Said to derive its name from teppo-ae, an old term after teppo (gun), a local nickname for the carp — a winter dish served alongside sake.
source_title: てっぱい 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Wakegiae — scallion and octopus dressed in vinegared white miso
summary_ja: ゆでたわけぎとゆでダコを、白味噌に酢や辛子を合わせた衣で和える春の惣菜。子孫繁栄の縁起物として雛祭りの頃に食べられてきたとされ、白味噌の甘い衣から「ぬたあえ」とも呼ばれる。
summary_en: Boiled scallion and boiled octopus are dressed in a paste of white miso, vinegar, and mustard for a spring side dish. Said to be eaten around the Girls' Festival as a symbol of a thriving family line, and also known as nuta-ae for its sweet miso dressing.
source_title: わけぎあえ 香川県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
